decisive_items: A 55-year-old man underwent right hemicolectomy for moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon
Thirteen months after surgery, follow-up CT revealed a 25 mm lesion in segment 8 of the liver
response.rationale: History of colorectal cancer and appearance of a new liver lesion are highly suggestive of metastasis

rejected.why: Absence of communication with the biliary tree and negative bile cytology do not strongly support intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
Portal vein tumor thrombus is a complication, not the primary diagnosis
Negative hepatitis serologies reduce the likelihood of hepatocellular carcinoma
Hepatocellular carcinoma with portal vein tumor thrombus is less likely given the patient's history of colorectal cancer
